To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the optimal fractionation scheme is not necessarily uniform over a week of treatment; (2) the optimal scheme is not necessarily the same for all tumour types, even if the tumour is characterized by the same LQ model parameters; (3) the optimal scheme depends on the constraints imposed on the normal tissues; (4) for some tumour types and some constraints the optimal solution is unique.
the optimal fractionation schedule is not necessarily uniform over time and is not necessarily unique.

the optimal radiotherapy treatment is not necessarily uniform, the optimal treatment depends on the values of the parameters of the LQ model, and the optimal treatment is not the same as that proposed by other researchers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mathematical modeling and optimization of radiotherapy treatment.

a mathematical formulation of a radiotherapy problem, with the analysis of the mathematical properties of the problem itself and, finally, with the application of the results to the solution of the problem.

the development of a mathematical model of radiation response of normal and tumour tissues, and with the study of the properties of the optimal solution of the corresponding nonlinear programming problem.

the optimal solution is unique, it does not necessarily correspond to uniform fractionation and, in the case of prevalent late constraint and absence of the incomplete-repair term, it corresponds to a fractionation scheme with a high number of fractions, with a decreasing dose per fraction and with a decreasing fractionation time.
the optimal fractionation scheme is not necessarily uniform and it is a function of the model parameters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the presence of repopulation, the optimal fractionation is not necessarily uniform, but it depends on the relative values of the model parameters.
the optimal fractionation scheme for a given patient depends on the patient’s parameters, the type of normal tissues to protect and the constraints on the normal tissues.
the optimal treatment is not necessarily uniform over a single week.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LQ model with exponential repopulation is a useful framework to study the radiotherapy problem, and that the optimal fractionation scheme is not necessarily uniform over a single week.
the fractionation scheme should be tailored to the patient, rather than being based on general rules.
